clue.text: Programme of the leading Chartists?

parts.note: the Chartists were 1830s political reformers, but here the word is read as people topping the music charts, and their programme is the BBC show of hit singles

explanation.surface: A question about the manifesto of the foremost Victorian Chartist reformers.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartists suggests the nineteenth-century campaigners; read it as acts at the head of the record charts.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC chart show featured the week's best-selling singles, so it was literally the programme of the chart leaders.

clue.text: Note river water falling to the ground

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
water falling from the sky is rain

explanation.surface: A memo about a river's water dropping onto the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, i.e. the ground.

clue.text: Noodles perhaps in Dad's Army

parts.note: pa is dad, with the possessive giving PA'S
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A suggestion that noodles feature in the British sitcom Dad's Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic BBC sitcom about Britain's wartime Home Guard; the TA is the Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are one kind of the Italian dough food, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Company meant to be dismantled? Heavens above!

parts.note: a firm is a business company

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart, so the letters of meant are pulled to pieces and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at a business that was meant to be broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, the heavens overhead.

clue.text: He succeeds, in their opinion

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words their opinion

explanation.surface: Someone is successful, at least in the view of others.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is a person who succeeds to a title or estate.

clue.text: Island home of Christian community

explanation.surface: An island where a Christian congregation lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is Fletcher Christian, leader of the Bounty mutineers, whose descendants settled the Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island is a remote landmass, and was the settlement of the mutineer Fletcher Christian and his followers.

clue.text: One's in a position to make an assumption

indicators.note: in signals that one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a post is a position or job; that the answer's letters also open the word position is a coincidence
One's gives I

explanation.surface: Someone well placed to suppose something.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition as a premise, i.e. to suppose.

clue.text: There's nothing right in the canal programme

indicators.note: in signals that the pieces are placed inside the canal's name

parts.note: the Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A claim that a canal TV programme is wholly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is the BBC's long-running current affairs series.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC current-affairs show of that name is a television programme.

clue.text: Pound for pound — uncommonly steep in the circumstances

indicators.note: circumstances surround something, so the letters of steep wrap round the other piece
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters of steep are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A remark that, pound for pound, something is unusually expensive given the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is a club-shaped tool used to crush or grind, and as a verb means to grind in a mortar.

clue.text: Check the others including followers

indicators.note: including means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: the rest are the others
a train is a retinue of followers

explanation.surface: Verify that the remaining people include some supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is a check or curb on action.

clue.text: Disgrace has shattered me

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of has and me are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonour has left the speaker crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame is dishonour or disgrace.

clue.text: Divine appearance of girl-sailor

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A heavenly vision of a female sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief an avatar is the descent of a deity to earth in bodily form, a god made manifest.

clue.text: Lights out to make a final appointment

explanation.surface: Switching off the lights to arrange one last meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Last Post is the bugle call sounded at night in British military camps.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call signals bedtime in barracks, and read literally the words mean a last job.

clue.text: Less sensitive figure

explanation.surface: A shape that feels less.
explanation.definitionFit: More numb means less able to feel, and the other reading is a digit or numeral.

clue.text: The first one raised by rioters

definitions.text: The first one raised by rioters

parts.words: The first one raised by rioters
parts.note: rioters are said to raise Cain, and Cain, who killed Abel, was the first to take a life in the Bible

explanation.surface: Something rioters were first to lift up.
explanation.walkthrough: To raise Cain is to cause a disturbance; Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain was the Bible's first killer, the one rioters raise in the idiom.

clue.text: Mark degrees of academic status

explanation.surface: Marking the grades of academic standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate a scale is to mark it in degrees, and a graduate holds a university degree.

clue.text: Vessel identified in the Indian Navy as "Kali"?

definitions.text: Vessel identified in the Indian Navy as "Kali"?

parts.words: Vessel identified in the Indian Navy as "Kali"?
parts.note: Kali is the Hindu goddess of destruction, so a warship named for her would be a type of fast naval escort named for wrecking

explanation.surface: A warship of the Indian Navy carrying the name of a Hindu goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast warship class and Kali's role in Hinduism, the annihilator, share one word.

clue.text: Stretch of wild glen to the north

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters of glen are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tract of untamed valley lying northward.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to make it longer.

clue.text: Sponsors certain matches

parts.note: sure means certain
ties are matches or games in a cup competition

explanation.surface: Backers of definite fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sureties are people who stand guarantee for another, i.e. sponsors.

clue.text: How to satisfy the plastic market?

definitions.text: How to satisfy the plastic market?

parts.words: How to satisfy the plastic market?
parts.note: a market is met by providing goods, and 'how plastic' asks for an adverb meaning in a pliant manner; one word does both jobs

explanation.surface: A business question about meeting demand for plastics.
explanation.walkthrough: The adverb from supple, meaning pliantly, can be spelt the same as the word for providing goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Providing goods meets demand in economics, and the rarer adverb means flexibly, as plastic things bend.

clue.text: In Africa does Tommy require fresh air?

parts.note: to ask is to require or demand

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new, so the letters of air are made over

explanation.surface: Asking whether a British soldier in Africa needs some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is slang for a British private soldier; the definition reads 'what in Africa does for a Tommy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari was a local soldier serving in colonial East Africa, the counterpart of the British private.

clue.text: Name one might hear at the Wailing Wall?

definitions.text: Name one might hear at the Wailing Wall?

parts.words: Name one might hear at the Wailing Wall?
parts.note: a Hebrew name from the Book of Samuel meaning the glory has departed, fit for lamenting at Jerusalem's Western Wall

explanation.surface: A question about a name heard at Jerusalem's Western Wall.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel the name is given to a child born as the Ark is captured, meaning 'the glory is departed'; the Wailing Wall is a site of lament.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical name is itself a lament, matching the mourning done at the Wailing Wall.

clue.text: Standing for president I get frustrated

indicators.note: frustrated means thwarted, so the letters of I get are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone running for president feels thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is status or high standing.

clue.text: An opera to look over? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely tells us the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to scan is to look over

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to skim an opera only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's work about a singer in Rome is a celebrated opera.

clue.text: Somehow the bar must be held underwater

indicators.note: somehow means by some unknown method, so the letters of the and bar are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somehow a bar has to be kept below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers must hold the air in their lungs when submerged.

clue.text: Farewell to Pearl Harbour could be

definitions.text: Farewell to Pearl Harbour could be

parts.words: Farewell to Pearl Harbour could be
parts.note: Pearl Harbour is in Hawaii, so a goodbye said there would be the Hawaiian greeting word

explanation.surface: A goodbye to the Hawaiian naval base.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word serves both as hello and goodbye.

clue.text: In Thackeray's book, he's a cobbler

explanation.surface: A character in a Thackeray novel is a shoemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Thackeray wrote The Book of Snobs; in old dialect the word also meant a shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's book catalogues social climbers, and the dialect sense is a shoemaker or apprentice.

clue.text: 51 3/4 rights of possession

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
three quarters are three of the compass points, here east, north and south

explanation.surface: A mysterious fraction heads a legal note about ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: The four quarters are the compass points, so three quarters gives three of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Workers' case for raising issue of the Queen is full of holes

definitions.text: Workers' case for raising issue of the Queen

explanation.surface: Workers' grounds for raising the Queen's children are full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers are worker bees, and the issue of the Queen is the queen bee's brood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees rear the queen's larvae in wax cells, and as a verb the word means to riddle with cavities.

clue.text: Pass needed for a dog

explanation.surface: A pass is needed for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great St Bernard Pass crosses the Alps between Switzerland and Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine pass gave its name to the large rescue-dog breed.
